Ghostty's maintainer kept a journal for a month marking an 'X' on every date a GitHub outage hurt his ability to work; almost every day had an X. He says Git isn't the problem, it's the infrastructure around it: issues, PRs, Actions.
User says GitHub has been 'infuriating lately' with outages, and its decline makes them sad.
Commenter says GitHub is visibly crumbling and points to an unofficial status page that 'tells a horrifying story' of outages. They think inertia is the only reason people haven't left.
Ghostty's maintainer says GitHub gave him so much and he truly loves it, but 'it's not what it used to be.' The team discussed leaving for months before deciding to move.

Users weighing alternatives to GitHub (Codeberg, self-hosted Forgejo, GitLab, SourceHut, Tangled) say the community is fracturing. Leaving GitHub means accounts everywhere and losing easy discovery of projects, since GitHub was 'the git community.'
Workaround suggested for leaving GitHub: use git-bug, which stores issues and PRs inside git refs and offers two-way sync with many providers, alongside moving to a forge like Codeberg.
Commenter recalls GitHub always having reliability problems in its early days. It was a famous Rails app with notorious, constant outages around 2008–2009.

Long-time user dislikes that GitHub is proprietary software that structurally locks users in despite being built on git. They also object that it requires accounts and doesn't work in Iran because of US sanctions compliance.
User says they switched from GitHub to GitLab after GitHub changed the default branch name from master to main.
Teacher says students pushing to GitHub Classroom with 'push -u origin master' were rejected and had to use main, causing a 'WTF moment' in class.
Complaint: because GitHub creates a default 'main' branch on repo creation, you either rename it or keep pushing to master by mistake and then redo the push to main 'every effing time.'

User thinks 'main' is a better name in principle, but says GitHub went too far by aggressively prompting devs to rename local master branches. They nearly renamed a former client's branch by accident.
User calls GitHub's search terribly bad. They say it's more efficient to clone a repo and use plain grep than to search code on GitHub.
User says they love GitHub but worry Microsoft will degrade it, citing a bad experience where a forced Skype account migration lost all their contacts.
Paying team customer asks GitHub to prioritize stability, saying their dev team and infrastructure get hit by GitHub outages 'seemingly every week,' often coinciding with new feature launches.
User notes that after the Team price cut, existing seats weren't automatically reduced. They had to manually downgrade from 5 seats to 3 to bring the bill to $12/month.

User lists what you lose downgrading from Team to Free on private repos: protected branches, draft PRs, Pages, wikis, code owners, multiple assignees, auto review assignment, and scheduled reminders. Actions minutes drop from 3,000 to 2,000 and package storage from 2GB to 500MB.
User who historically wasn't a fan of GitHub says the pace of innovation since the Microsoft acquisition has been really impressive.
User who spread repos across GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket depending on team size and features says free teams lets them centralize everything on GitHub.

User who moved to GitLab when GitHub changed pricing says GitLab offered free CI/CD well before Actions and they 'never looked back.' Another says GitHub would need self-hosted runners for organizations to beat GitLab for teams.
